subject: Estimating Factor Scores for an Orthogonal Model

messages.author: 7c5c124542efbd3f
messages.subject: Estimating Factor Scores for an Orthogonal Model
parts:
Hello, 

When trying to estimate factor scores for an orthogonal model using lavaan, I noticed that the factor scores end up being substantially correlated anyway (though correlations are higher in magnitude if the model is not orthogonal).  I'm wondering whether this behavior is expected or I've made some mistake in how I'm estimating factor scores.  I noticed the same pattern with plausible values as well.  The below code will demonstrate these correlations.  Any clarity would be greatly appreciated.  Thank you!


library(lavaan)
library(psych)

## fit model
HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, orthogonal = TRUE)

### in R
fs <- lavPredict(fit, method = "regression")

### R plausible values
pv <- plausibleValues(fit)
pv.1 <- pv[[2]]
colnames(pv.1) <- c("ID.pv", "visual.pv", "textual.pv", "speed.pv")
pv.1 <- pv.1[, 2:4]

### bind all the columns
total <- cbind(fs, pv.1)
# correlations among variables
cor.plot(total, upper = FALSE)

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Estimating Factor Scores for an Orthogonal Model
parts:
This doesn't answer your question, but why are you using orthogonal=TRUE? In a CFA it makes little sense to me, because the factor covariances are what they are, and even in EFA orthogonal rotations are largely obsolete.

How well does the orthogonal model fit?

Pat

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Estimating Factor Scores for an Orthogonal Model
parts:
"Regression" factor scores (and "Bartlett" factor scores) do NOT
preserve the correlation structure among the latent variables.

For a discussion, see

Berge, J., Krijnen, W., Wansbeek, T., & Shapiro, A. (1999). SOME NEW
RESULTS ON CORRELATION-PRESERVING FACTOR SCORES PREDICTION METHODS.
Linear Algebra and its Applications, 289, 311-318.

Yves.
